title: API 510 Training in Los Angeles: Vessel Inspector Exam Prep
description: Self-paced API 510 exam prep for Los Angeles: coke drums, FCC and hydroprocessing vessels at South Bay refineries, Cal/OSHA rules, instructor Q&A.
h1: API 510 Training in Los Angeles: Online Exam Prep for South Bay Refinery Vessel Inspectors
html:
API 510 exam prep for pressure vessel inspectors in the Los Angeles basin

Most of the pressure vessels an API 510 inspector looks after in Southern California sit in a short strip of the South Bay and the harbour district: refinery columns, coke drums, reactors, separators and exchanger shells in El Segundo, Torrance, Carson and Wilmington. This page is for the people who inspect them or want to: refinery and contractor NDT technicians, welding inspectors, operators moving into inspection, and engineers who approve inspection plans.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Los Angeles. Atlantis has offices in Houston and Hyderabad, and its API 510 course is self-paced and online, with an instructor who answers your questions as you work through the codes. The American Petroleum Institute (API) decides whether you are eligible, administers the examination in person at Prometric test centres and issues the certification, and you apply to API yourself. Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider, so treat the course as preparation for API's exam rather than a step in API's process.

Four large refineries, and the vessels inside them

The Energy Information Administration's refinery capacity survey, with data as of January 2026, lists five operating refineries in the Los Angeles area. Four are large, and each of the four runs a delayed coker and a fluid catalytic cracker, which tells an API 510 candidate a great deal about the vessels waiting for them.

The California Energy Commission notes that Marathon's Carson and Wilmington plants have reported as one refinery since 2019, so a single inspection department may hold the records for equipment on both sides of what used to be a property line. Phillips 66 stopped processing crude at its own Los Angeles refinery, which also had sites in Carson and Wilmington, in October 2025, and the company has hired developers to study what the land could be used for next. Pressure vessels also sit outside the refinery fences: Air Products runs hydrogen production facilities in Wilmington and Carson, and a hydrogen plant's shift converters, separators and pressure swing adsorption beds, which cycle pressure all day, bring fatigue into an inspector's thinking.

Coke drums, FCC vessels and hydroprocessing reactors

A delayed coker gives its vessel inspectors some of the hardest-worked pressure equipment in any refinery. Each drum is filled with hot residue, steamed, quenched with water and opened for cutting, cycle after cycle, and the repeated thermal strain shows up as bulging of the shell and cracking at circumferential seams and at the skirt attachment weld. Inspectors track bulges with laser profiling and examine the skirt weld with magnetic particle or ultrasonic methods.

FCC reactors, regenerators and main fractionators raise different questions: refractory linings that protect the shell until they crack or spall, erosion from circulating catalyst, hot spots that an infrared survey picks up between turnarounds, and high-temperature damage in the hottest sections. Catalytic hydrocrackers, which EIA lists at three of the four large refineries, add thick-walled chromium-molybdenum reactors and high-pressure exchangers in hydrogen service, where high temperature hydrogen attack is screened against API RP 941 and ammonium bisulfide corrodes the reactor effluent cooling train.

Not all of this is exam material. The API 510 Body of Knowledge draws on a short list of RP 571 damage mechanisms, among them high temperature hydrogen attack, sulfidation, wet H2S damage, amine cracking, chloride stress corrosion cracking, corrosion under insulation and brittle fracture, and it tests them the way an inspector meets them: what the damage looks like, which materials and conditions make a vessel susceptible, and which methods find it. Coke drum fatigue is not examined as a topic, but drum experience teaches why a plan names the mechanism before it picks the method.

Who decides how a Los Angeles vessel is inspected

Two state rules sit beside the code. Cal/OSHA's Pressure Vessel Unit issues permits to operate for air tanks above 1.5 cubic feet, LP-gas tanks above 125 gallons of water capacity and power boilers above 15 psig, and the permit inspections are made by its own inspectors or by qualified inspectors employed by insurance companies. A refinery's process columns, drums and exchangers are handled through a different route. Title 8, section 5189.1, Cal/OSHA's process safety management standard for petroleum refineries, operative since October 2017, requires inspections and tests on process equipment to follow procedures that meet or exceed recognized and generally accepted good engineering practice, and its definitions name API among the organisations whose publications count.

Section 5189.1 also wants a certification record for each inspection and test, giving the date, the name of the person who performed it, a description of the work, the results and an equipment identifier, and the employer has to correct deficiencies so that equipment stays safe to operate. Those are much the same items API 510 expects in an inspection record, which is one reason South Bay owner-users value inspectors who write reports a regulator can follow line by line. The rule does not name API 510 or any certification; each owner decides what its own inspectors and its contractors must hold. For the federal and state background, see PSM, RAGAGEP and the API inspection codes.

The refinery inspection departments here work as owner-user inspection organisations, adding contract inspectors and NDT crews for turnarounds. API 510's definition of an authorized inspection agency includes the owner-user's own inspection organisation, so time in a refinery inspection department, or with a contractor working for one, is the kind of experience API looks for in an application.

Damage a Los Angeles vessel inspector looks for

  • Wet H2S damage. Sour water strippers, amine units, coker and FCC gas plants and their overhead accumulators can develop blistering, hydrogen induced cracking and stress-oriented cracking near welds. Thickness readings do not find it; wet fluorescent magnetic particle and angle-beam ultrasonic examination do.
  • Amine cracking. Absorbers, regenerators and their exchangers in lean or rich amine, especially at welds that were never stress relieved.
  • Sulfidation. Hot sections of crude, vacuum and coker fractionators handling sulfur-bearing streams, where the rate depends on temperature, sulfur content and alloy.
  • Corrosion under insulation and external chloride cracking. Insulated vessels close to the harbour breathe salt-laden marine air, and insulated austenitic stainless steel at the wrong temperature can crack from the outside.
  • Brittle fracture. Older thick-walled carbon steel vessels during a hydrotest or a cold restart, which is why MDMT and impact test exemption rules matter even in a mild climate.

Seismic design shapes every California vessel, from skirt and anchor bolt details to the supports of tall columns, but the API 510 Body of Knowledge leaves wind and seismic load calculations out of the examination. Learn the inspection side for your job and leave the seismic arithmetic to the design engineers.

Worked example: a sour water feed drum that passes on thickness

These figures are for practice and describe no real vessel. A horizontal feed drum in sour water service has an inside radius of 36 in., a design pressure of 150 psi, an allowable stress of 17,500 psi given in the problem and a joint efficiency of 0.85. Its lowest shell reading was 0.625 in. sixteen years ago, 0.565 in. six years ago and 0.530 in. at the latest inspection.

  1. Required thickness under UG-27(c)(1): t = PR ÷ (SE − 0.6P) = 5,400 ÷ 14,785 = 0.365 in.
  2. Long-term rate = (0.625 − 0.530) ÷ 16 = 0.0059 in. per year. Short-term rate = (0.565 − 0.530) ÷ 6 = 0.0058 in. per year. The long-term rate is the higher of the two here.
  3. Remaining life = (0.530 − 0.365) ÷ 0.0059 = about 28 years.
  4. Internal or on-stream interval = the lesser of half the remaining life and 10 years, which is 10 years.
  5. MAWP at the end of that interval: 0.530 − 2 × 0.0059 × 10 = 0.412 in., and MAWP = SEt ÷ (R + 0.6t) = 14,875 × 0.412 ÷ 36.247 = about 169 psi, comfortably above the 150 psi design pressure.

On thickness alone the drum looks healthy, and that is the trap. Wet H2S cracking has no corrosion rate, so a ten-year interval worked out from wall loss says nothing about whether blistering or stepwise cracking has started beside the welds. API 510 expects an inspection plan to take account of the damage mechanisms that apply, which here means crack-detection examination of the welds and a reasoned decision on whether on-stream inspection can stand in for an internal look. Exam questions often follow the same pattern: they supply the numbers, then ask something the numbers cannot answer.

Routes into API 510 from Los Angeles jobs

API weighs education against pressure vessel experience gained in the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency. With a bachelor's degree in engineering or technology you need one year supervising or performing vessel inspection; with a two-year degree or certificate, two years of vessel experience; with a high school diploma, three; and with no formal education, five or more, each route including at least one year of inspection. See the API 510 certification requirements for the detail. Typical starting points here:

  • Refinery and contractor UT technicians who have taken thickness readings on columns, drums and exchangers through several turnarounds. Atlantis's NDT training in Los Angeles page covers the earlier ASNT steps.
  • Welders and welding inspectors from maintenance contractors and fabrication shops, whose repair work counts as vessel experience once it sits alongside a year of inspection. The AWS CWI exam prep page for Los Angeles covers the welding inspector route.
  • Aerospace NDT technicians. Southern California trains many NDT technicians for aircraft and space work. Their method skill transfers, but API counts experience on pressure vessels, so hours on airframe parts do not meet the requirement. Plan a move into vessel inspection before you apply.
  • Operators, maintenance supervisors and graduate engineers who have run, repaired or approved work on the equipment and then joined the inspection group.

Studying API 510 around South Bay turnarounds

Self-paced study suits a workforce that moves between day shifts, nights and twelve-hour turnaround rotations. Pick an exam window that falls between your site's big outages, then work backwards. Start with API 510 itself, because the closed-book half leans on it; build the Section VIII calculations until you can do them without looking anything up; then add RP 571, RP 572, RP 576, RP 577 and RP 578, followed by Section IX, Section V and the PCC-2 repair articles. During a turnaround, keep a short daily habit of practice questions rather than stopping entirely.

Write down the questions your own job raises. If a coke drum report uses a term you cannot place in the code, or a coworker's interval does not match yours, send it to the instructor. The API 510 practice questions and the API 510 code overview are useful companions.

Preparation options in Los Angeles, compared

  • Intensive seminars run by training companies before an exam window suit candidates who already know the codes and can take consecutive days away from site. Ask whether the material follows the effectivity sheet for your window and who answers questions after the seminar ends.
  • Employer programmes. Large owner-users sometimes run internal study groups or mentoring for candidates. Ask your inspection supervisor before paying for anything yourself.
  • College programmes. Cerritos College in Norwalk runs a welding programme with AWS Certified Welding Inspectors on its staff and certificates that include pipe welding, a strong grounding for RP 577 and Section IX. It is not API exam preparation, and it does not claim to be.
  • Self-paced online study with instructor Q&A, which is how Atlantis delivers its API 510 course. It suits candidates on rotating shifts and those who need to repeat the calculations several times.

Whichever you choose, the examination is the same: API holds it in person, and Prometric lists test centres in and around Los Angeles. Freeway traffic around the basin is unpredictable, so book a seat you can reach without a long morning drive.

Sponsoring API 510 candidates from a Los Angeles refinery or contractor

Refinery inspection departments and the contractors that staff South Bay turnarounds often sponsor two or three candidates together, sometimes mixing an experienced UT technician with a young engineer. Because each person works at their own pace, nobody waits for the slowest member of a group. Check each candidate's experience record against API's rules before enrolling them, since eligibility is personal and no course changes it. Fees are quoted on request for one candidate or several, and Atlantis can also prepare candidates for API 570 and API 653 where your team covers piping and tankage as well as vessels.

faq.q: Is there an API 510 class I can attend in person in Los Angeles?
faq.a: Atlantis does not run one: there is no Atlantis classroom in Los Angeles, and the API 510 course is self-paced online study with instructor Q&A. Whichever route you take, API holds the examination in person at a Prometric test centre once it accepts your application.

faq.q: Does Cal/OSHA require refinery vessel inspectors to hold API 510?
faq.a: Section 5189.1 does not name API 510 or any other certification. It requires inspections and tests that meet or exceed recognized and generally accepted good engineering practice and lists API among the recognized organisations. South Bay refiners generally meet that requirement through API 510 programmes, so the owner sets the certification it expects from its own inspectors and from contractors.

faq.q: I am an aerospace NDT technician in Southern California. Does my experience count toward API 510?
faq.a: Your NDT skill transfers, but API counts experience in the design, construction, repair, operation or inspection of pressure vessels, gained with an authorized inspection agency, including at least one year supervising or performing vessel inspection. Work on airframe or engine components does not meet that requirement. Many technicians move into refinery or contractor vessel work first and apply once their record qualifies.

faq.q: Are coke drums on the API 510 exam?
faq.a: Coke drums are pressure vessels, so the API 510 rules for inspection, repair and rerating apply to them, but the Body of Knowledge does not single them out. The exam tests API 510, the listed RP 571 mechanisms, Section VIII calculations and the other listed documents. Experience on drums helps because it teaches you to link a mechanism to an inspection method, which many questions ask you to do.

faq.q: Do I need to learn seismic design for the API 510 exam if I work in California?
faq.a: No. The Body of Knowledge excludes wind and seismic load calculations, along with external pressure, flange and tubesheet design. California vessels are designed for earthquakes, and an in-service inspector should look for damaged anchor bolts, skirts and supports after a strong event, but the examination does not ask you to calculate seismic loads.

faq.q: Is there still API 510 work in Los Angeles after the Phillips 66 closure?
faq.a: Yes. EIA's January 2026 survey still lists four large refineries in the area, each with cokers, fluid catalytic crackers and the columns, drums and exchangers that go with them, plus a small refinery at South Gate. Hydrogen plants and the contractors serving all of these sites also employ vessel inspectors.

faq.q: Where do Los Angeles candidates sit the API 510 exam?
faq.a: At a Prometric test centre, in person. Prometric lists test centres in and around Los Angeles; choose one when you schedule after API approves your application. The day runs about 7.5 hours, with a closed-book part, a lunch break and an open-book part on screen, and you may not bring books or notes. The exam windows and deadlines are on the API exam schedule page.
